bugs.name: Long milestone titles overlap repository labels in the global milestone list at 390×844
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, a long milestone title overlaps its repository label in the global milestone list.
bugs.expected: Milestone titles and repository labels remain separately readable.
bugs.actual: The long title overlaps and obscures the eval/harbor-handbook repository label, including after filtering to Open and sorting by Name.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and create an open milestone named mo-milestones-small-viewport-390-20260614-1812-q3x in eval/harbor-handbook.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and open /milestones.
Select Open and sort by Name.
Inspect the long milestone row; its title overlaps the repository label and remains overlapped after waiting five seconds.

bugs.name: Global milestones: Sort > Name discards the repository filter and restores excluded milestones
bugs.summary: Sorting global milestones by Name clears the active repository selection and restores milestones from excluded repositories.
bugs.expected: Name sorting should reorder only milestones in the selected repositories, retaining the active repository selection and excluding milestones from deselected repositories.
bugs.actual: After deselecting eval/harbor-handbook, the global list shows 2 Open milestones. Sort > Name removes repos from the URL, resets the sidebar selection, and shows 3 Open including the previously excluded Handbook 1.1 milestone.
reproSteps: Sign in as fixture administrator eval. Through the UI, ensure at least two accessible repositories have open milestones; create disposable repositories/milestones if necessary.
Open the global /milestones dashboard. Deselect one repository in the sidebar and confirm its milestone disappears while another repository remains selected.
Open Sort and choose Name.
Observe that the repository selection resets, the URL loses repos, and the excluded milestone returns. In the native reproduction the count increased from 2 Open to 3 Open.

matchingGuidance.deduplication: Distinct from gitea-milestone-search-sort-reset (repository search drops sorting) and gitea-pass2-004 (rejected multiselect interpretation). This reference requires a verified excluded repository returning after global Name sorting.

bugs.name: Milestone search clears the selected due-date sort
bugs.summary: Searching milestones clears the selected Latest due date sort and shows the future-due milestone after the past-due milestone.
bugs.expected: After selecting Latest due date and searching QA, retain sort=furthestduedate and show the latest-due QA milestone before the past-due one, with undated milestones afterward.
bugs.actual: The search navigated to /eval/harbor-handbook/milestones?state=open&q=QA, dropping sort=furthestduedate. The visible filtered rows put undated QA Alpha first, QA Beta Past (Oct 1, 2026) before QA Gamma Future (Feb 28, 2027). This persisted in the reviewed recording.
reproSteps: Sign in as fixture user eval and open the repository Milestones page for eval/harbor-handbook. Through New Milestone, create three uniquely suffixed open milestones: QA Alpha Updated - QA-01 with no due date, QA Beta Past - QA-01 due 2026-10-01, and QA Gamma Future - QA-01 due 2027-02-28.

Open Sort and select Latest due date. Confirm that the URL contains sort=furthestduedate and that QA Gamma Future appears before QA Beta Past, with undated milestones afterward. This applies the sort before searching.
Enter QA in the milestone search field and press Enter.

Inspect the resulting URL and rows. The search URL contains state=open&q=QA but no sort parameter; undated QA Alpha rows appear first, and QA Beta Past appears before QA Gamma Future. Searching has reset the applied ordering.
bugs.sourceCause: Repository milestones use the shared issue search form, whose hidden sort input is inside the not PageIsMilestones condition. The milestone handler sets PageIsMilestones=true, so normal search submission sends state and q without the applied sort. The handler then passes an empty SortType to the milestone query, changing deadline_unix DESC to the default deadline_unix ASC, name ASC. This reverses dated rows and moves undated zero-deadline rows first.

bugs.name: Milestone due date January 1, 1970 renders as '-' despite being saved
bugs.summary: A saved January 1, 1970 milestone deadline displays a dash in the milestone list even though Edit retains the date.
bugs.expected: The milestone list should display the saved January 1, 1970 deadline as a date, consistently with other saved deadlines; it should not substitute a dash.
bugs.actual: The list shows a calendar icon followed by '-' for the milestone. Opening Edit shows the saved Due Date as 01/01/1970.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval in the fixture default UTC environment and open a writable repository’s Milestones > New Milestone.
Create a uniquely named milestone with Due Date January 1, 1970.
Inspect its row in the milestone list: the calendar icon is followed by '-' rather than the date.
Open Edit Milestone and confirm the saved Due Date remains January 1, 1970.

matchingGuidance.scope: Default UTC fixture display path. No lost date or identical behavior in every timezone is claimed.

bugs.name: Milestone All issues retains the implicit Assigned to you filter
bugs.summary: Returning the milestone Type filter from Assigned to you to All issues preserves an assignee restriction that the first selection injected, so previously visible open items remain hidden.
bugs.expected: Choosing All issues reverses the restriction introduced by Assigned to you and restores the milestone’s previously visible items when no independent Assignee filter was selected.
bugs.actual: At 390×844, the milestone initially displayed two open items, issue #4 and PR #5. Assigned to you showed no results. Selecting All issues still showed 0 Open, 0 Closed, and No results after five seconds; the URL contained type=all and assignee=1 despite no independent Assignee selection.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. Create a disposable milestone and two open issues in a writable repository. Select that milestone in each issue’s Milestone picker, leaving both issues unassigned.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and open the milestone detail. With no independent Assignee filter selected, confirm both open items are visible.
Open the Type filter and choose Assigned to you. Confirm the unassigned items disappear.
In the same Type filter, choose All issues. Wait five seconds and observe that the items remain hidden and the URL includes type=all with an assignee parameter for the signed-in user.

bugs.name: Closing a milestone opens an empty closed-milestone list
bugs.summary: Closing the milestone redirects to a list URL with `state=close`; the page reports one closed milestone but renders no row until the Closed filter changes the URL to `state=closed`.
bugs.expected: After closing the milestone, the closed-milestone list should display the milestone consistently with its closed count, without requiring the user to select the Closed filter again.
bugs.actual: The close action landed at /eval/mo-gitea-03-issues-milestones-close-repro/milestones?state=close. The page showed “1 Closed” but no milestone row. Selecting “1 Closed” navigated to /eval/mo-gitea-03-issues-milestones-close-repro/milestones?state=closed and displayed the milestone row.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval.
Create a fresh repository named `mo-gitea-03-issues-milestones-close-repro` through the UI.
Open the repository’s Issues > Milestones page and create a milestone titled `mo-gitea-03-issues-close-repro-milestone`.
Open that milestone’s detail page and click its Close action.
On the resulting page at /eval/mo-gitea-03-issues-milestones-close-repro/milestones?state=close, observe “1 Closed” and no milestone row; the state remained visible after five seconds.
Click the visible “1 Closed” filter. At /eval/mo-gitea-03-issues-milestones-close-repro/milestones?state=closed, observe the milestone row.
bugs.sourceCause: routers/web/repo/milestone.go ChangeMilestoneStatus redirects to /milestones?state=<action>, so Close sends state=close, while the Milestones page only treats state=closed as the Closed view and shows the Open list for anything else.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reports that closing a milestone (from its details page or the list, however the page was reached) lands on state=close, the Open view, an empty list, or a list without the just-closed milestone match this entry, unless the report's observed result says the repository tabs, header or page body disappeared; those match gitea-milestone-close-blanks-page instead.

bugs.name: Whitespace-only titles create milestones with invisible detail links
bugs.summary: A milestone title made only of spaces passes the required-title check, is trimmed to an empty name, and is saved, leaving a milestone whose title link, detail heading, and picker entry are blank.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only milestone title is rejected like an empty one, as Gitea does for issue, release, and wiki titles.
bugs.actual: Creating a milestone titled with spaces succeeds with 'The milestone " " has been created.' The list shows a zero-size, unclickable title link, the detail page has an empty heading, and the issue sidebar's milestone picker shows a nameless entry. Editing an existing milestone's title to spaces does the same.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture account and open a repository's Issues → Milestones → New Milestone.
Enter three spaces as the title and choose Create Milestone.
Observe the success message and the increased open count.
Observe the new row has no visible title link, and opening it by URL shows an empty heading.
As a control, submit an empty title and observe the browser blocks it with "Please fill out this field."

bugs.name: Accented milestone search lists matches but the Open/Closed counters read zero
bugs.summary: On SQLite, milestone search matches accented keywords with ASCII-only uppercasing, but the Open/Closed counters uppercase the keyword fully, so an accented search like café lists matching milestones under tabs that read 0 Open / 0 Closed.
bugs.expected: The Open and Closed counters count the same milestones the search lists, as they do for unaccented keywords.
bugs.actual: Searching closed milestones for 'café' lists the matching closed milestones, but the tabs read 0 Open and 0 Closed, including after reload. Searching 'caf' lists the same rows with the correct Closed count. The global Milestones page shows the same zero counters, and its pagination follows them, so with more than one page of accented matches the Next link is missing.
reproSteps: Open a repository's Milestones page and create a milestone whose title contains 'café', then close it.
Select Closed and search for 'café'.
Observe the milestone is listed but the tabs read 0 Open and 0 Closed.
Search for 'caf' instead and observe the same milestone with a Closed count of 1.

bugs.name: Unbroken milestone titles overflow the mobile milestone list and detail pages
bugs.summary: Milestone titles render without any word-break rule, so a long title with no spaces or hyphens (up to the form's 50-character limit) widens the repository milestone list and the milestone detail page past a 390px viewport, forcing horizontal scrolling.
bugs.expected: A milestone title the form accepts wraps within a 390px viewport on the repository milestone list and the milestone detail page, as hyphenated titles and Projects titles do.
bugs.actual: At 390×844, a 50-character unbroken title makes the repository milestone list about 430–480px wide with the title clipped at the edge, and the milestone detail page about 625–707px wide with its heading running off screen. Both persist after reload and need horizontal scrolling to read. A hyphenated 50-character title fits, and tablet and desktop widths are fine.
reproSteps: Create a milestone whose title is 50 characters with no spaces or hyphens, e.g. 'WWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW'.
Set the viewport to 390×844 and open the repository's Milestones list.
Observe the page scrolls horizontally and the title runs past the right edge.
Open the milestone's detail page and observe the heading widens the page well past 390px.

relatedReference.name: Long milestone titles overlap repository labels in the global milestone list at 390×844
relatedReference.distinction: Both come from milestone titles having no word-break at mobile width, but on different pages with different symptoms: this reference covers the repository milestone list and milestone detail page widening the page into horizontal scroll, and the related reference covers the global /milestones list where the title overlaps the repository label. Credit each finding to the reference for the page and symptom it reports.

bugs.name: Closing or reopening a milestone from a searched list clears the search and sort
bugs.summary: The milestone list's Close and Open (reopen) actions redirect to the list with only a state parameter, so a search keyword and sort selected on the list are discarded and unrelated milestones reappear.
bugs.expected: After closing or reopening a milestone from a searched, sorted list, the list keeps the search keyword and sort, as the list's own Open/Closed tabs do.
bugs.actual: Searching the milestone list, sorting by Latest due date, and clicking Close on a result lands on /milestones?state=close with an empty search box, the default sort, and non-matching open milestones listed. Reopening a milestone from a searched Closed list likewise lands on /milestones?state=open without the search or sort.
reproSteps: Create several milestones whose titles share a prefix, plus one milestone that doesn't match.
On the repository's Milestones page, search for the shared prefix and choose Sort > Latest due date.
Click Close on one of the matching milestones.
Observe the search box is empty, the sort is reset, and the non-matching milestone is listed.
Switch to Closed, search again, click Open on the closed milestone, and observe the search is lost the same way.

relatedReference.name: Closing a milestone opens an empty closed-milestone list
relatedReference.distinction: Both come from the milestone status-change redirect, but they are different defects: this reference covers losing the search keyword and sort after Close or Reopen from a searched list (Reopen sends the correct state and still loses them), and the related reference covers the redirect using state=close so the Closed list is not shown. Credit search/sort-loss findings here and empty-closed-list findings to the related reference.

bugs.name: Deleting a milestone from a searched list clears the search, sort and state
bugs.summary: Deleting a milestone from the milestone list always redirects to the bare Milestones page, so the search keyword, sort, and Open/Closed state selected on the list are discarded and unrelated milestones reappear.
bugs.expected: After deleting a milestone from a searched, sorted list, the list keeps the search keyword, sort and selected state.
bugs.actual: Searching the milestone list, sorting by Latest due date, and deleting a matching milestone succeeds but lands on /milestones with an empty search box, the default sort, and non-matching milestones listed. Deleting from the Closed tab also returns to the Open tab.
reproSteps: Create several milestones whose titles share a prefix, plus one milestone that doesn't match.
On the repository's Milestones page, search for the shared prefix and choose Sort > Latest due date.
Click Delete on one of the matching milestones and confirm.
Observe the search box is empty, the sort is reset, and the non-matching milestone is listed.

relatedReference.distinction: Both lose the milestone list's search and sort after an action, but through different handlers: this reference covers Delete (which redirects to the bare Milestones page), and the related reference covers Close and Reopen (which redirect with only a state parameter). Credit each finding to the reference for the action it reports.

bugs.name: Milestone due date January 1, 0001 renders as '-' despite being saved
bugs.summary: A milestone due date of 0001-01-01 saves and reopens in the editor, but every milestone view shows a red calendar icon and '-' instead of the date, because the date re-parses to Go's zero time, which the date formatter treats as no date.
bugs.expected: A saved due date of January 1, 0001 is displayed as that date on the milestone list, detail page and global Milestones dashboard.
bugs.actual: Saving 01/01/0001 as a milestone's due date succeeds and Edit shows 0001-01-01, but the repository milestone list, milestone detail page and global Milestones dashboard show a red calendar icon followed by '-'. Neighboring dates such as 0001-01-02 and ordinary dates render correctly.
reproSteps: Create or edit a milestone and set its due date to 01/01/0001.
Save and reopen Edit to confirm the date is stored as 0001-01-01.
Open the repository's Milestones list and observe '-' instead of the date.

relatedReference.distinction: Both come from the date formatter treating a special instant as 'no date', but for different dates: this reference covers January 1, 0001 (Go's zero time), and the related reference covers January 1, 1970 (Unix zero). Credit each finding to the reference for the date it reports.

bugs.name: Milestone Type Assigned to you ignores the Assignee filter
bugs.summary: With the milestone Type filter set to Assigned to you, choosing an Assignee option such as Assigned to nobody updates the URL but leaves the list filtered only to the signed-in user, so contradictory filters show the user’s own assigned issues.
bugs.expected: An explicit Assignee selection is honored together with Type Assigned to you (Assigned to nobody shows no results), or the conflicting option is cleared or disabled so the list never contradicts the selected filters.
bugs.actual: In a milestone with issue #1 assigned to eval and issue #2 unassigned, Type Assigned to you listed only #1. Choosing Assignee, then Assigned to nobody, changed the URL to type=assigned&assignee=(none) but still listed #1 with 1 Open. On a fresh milestone page with Type All issues, the same Assigned to nobody choice listed only #2.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. In a writable repository, create a milestone with two open issues: one assigned to eval and one with no assignee.
Open the milestone detail page and confirm both issues are listed.
Open the Type filter and choose Assigned to you. Confirm only the issue assigned to eval is listed.
Open the Assignee filter and choose Assigned to nobody. Observe that the URL contains assignee=(none) but the issue assigned to eval is still listed.

relatedReference.distinction: gitea-pass2-005 is switching Type back to All issues and keeping the assignee=<you> restriction that Assigned to you injected. This entry is choosing an explicit Assignee option (Assigned to nobody, Assigned to anybody, or another user) while Type stays Assigned to you, and the list ignoring that Assignee choice.

bugs.name: Milestone Type Created by you ignores the Author filter
bugs.summary: With the milestone Type filter set to Created by you, choosing another user in the Author filter updates the URL and shows that user as the selected Author, but the list stays filtered to the signed-in user's own issues, so contradictory filters show issues the selected author did not open.
bugs.expected: An explicit Author selection is honored together with Type Created by you (Author alex shows no issues opened by eval), or the conflicting option is cleared or disabled so the list never contradicts the selected filters.
bugs.actual: In a milestone with issue #1 opened by eval and issue #2 opened by alex, Author alex with Type All issues (poster=alex) listed only #2. With Type Created by you and Author alex (type=created_by&poster=alex), the Author dropdown still had alex selected and Created by you was active, but the list showed only #1, opened by eval, with 1 Open.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. In a repository where alex can open issues, create a milestone with two open issues: one opened by eval and one opened by alex.
Open the milestone detail page and confirm both issues are listed.
Open the Type filter and choose Created by you. Confirm only the issue opened by eval is listed.
Open the Author filter and choose alex. Observe that the URL contains poster=alex and the Author filter shows alex, but the issue opened by eval is still listed and the issue opened by alex is not.

relatedReference.distinction: gitea-milestone-assigned-to-you-ignores-assignee-filter is the Assignee filter being ignored while Type is Assigned to you. This entry is the Author filter being ignored while Type is Created by you, so the list shows the signed-in user's own issues instead of the selected author's.

bugs.name: Milestone Sort > Name orders milestones Z to A
bugs.summary: Choosing Sort > Name on the repository or global Milestones list orders milestones in reverse alphabetical order, with no option for A to Z. Nothing breaks and the order is consistent, but a plain Name sort running Z to A is unintuitive.
bugs.expected: Sort > Name lists milestones alphabetically, A to Z (for example, Shared Release before Zebra Beta Release), as Gitea’s other unlabeled name sorts do, or the option is labelled to show it sorts in reverse.
bugs.actual: On the global Milestones page, searching a shared prefix and choosing Sort > Name gave Zebra, Mango, Banana, Apple, strictly Z to A across repositories; the repository Milestones list gave the same reverse order. The comparison is case-sensitive, so lowercase names sort above uppercase ones (asdf above Handbook above CROSS-Zebra above CROSS-Shared). The default sort lists the same undated milestones A to Z.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. In a writable repository, create milestones named Apple, Banana, Mango and Zebra with no due dates.
Open the repository Milestones page and confirm the default order is Apple, Banana, Mango, Zebra.
Open Sort and choose Name.
Observe the order Zebra, Mango, Banana, Apple.

relatedReference.distinction: gitea-global-milestone-name-sort-drops-repositories is Sort > Name on the global Milestones page discarding the repository filter and bringing back excluded milestones. This entry is the order Sort > Name produces (reverse alphabetical, case-sensitive) on the repository or global list, regardless of filters.

bugs.name: Clicking an issue’s label on a milestone page drops the Project, Sort and Author filters
bugs.summary: On a milestone detail page, clicking a label chip on an issue row keeps the search, Type, state and Assignee filters but drops the selected Project, Sort and Author, so the list widens to issues the user had filtered out.
bugs.expected: Clicking an issue’s label adds that label filter while preserving the other selected filters, including Project, Sort and Author, as the filter bar’s own Label dropdown does.
bugs.actual: In a milestone with issue A in project Roadmap and issue B in no project, both labelled bug, choosing Project → Roadmap listed only A with project=2 in the URL. Clicking the bug chip on A’s row navigated to ?q=&type=all&state=open&labels=4&assignee=&poster= and listed both A and B. With sort=oldest the chosen order was also lost. Choosing Label → bug from the filter bar instead kept project=2 and listed only A.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. In a writable repository, create a label, a project and a milestone.
Create two open issues in the milestone, both with the label: issue A assigned to the project and issue B with no project.
Open the milestone detail page, open the Project filter and choose the project. Confirm only issue A is listed.
Click the label chip on issue A’s row. Observe that the URL no longer contains project and issue B is listed again.

bugs.name: Long repository badges overlap the milestone title on mobile organization and global milestone lists
bugs.summary: At a 390px-wide viewport, a milestone row whose repository name is long shrinks the repository badge, but the badge text keeps painting past it over the milestone icon and title.
bugs.expected: The repository badge and milestone title wrap or truncate within their own space and stay readable on mobile.
bugs.actual: On an organization’s Milestones page at 390×844, a repository named with 62 characters produced a 261px badge whose text ran 240px past its edge, painting over a 106×17px area of the milestone icon and title. A short repository name in the same list did not overlap, and the long row did not overlap at 1280px.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval. Create an organization with one repository that has a long name (about 60 characters) and one with a short name, and create an open milestone in each.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and open the organization’s Milestones page.
Compare the two milestone heading rows. Observe that the long repository badge text runs over the milestone icon and title, while the short one does not.

relatedReference.name: Long milestone titles overlap repository labels in the global milestone list at 390×844
relatedReference.distinction: That entry is a long milestone title overflowing onto the repository label. This entry is the opposite element: a long repository badge overflowing onto the milestone icon and title.

bugs.name: Creating an issue whose selected milestone was deleted shows a raw JSON SyntaxError
bugs.summary: If the milestone selected on an unsaved New Issue draft is deleted elsewhere, clicking Create Issue shows a 'Network error SyntaxError … is not valid JSON' toast instead of saying the milestone no longer exists.
bugs.expected: Create Issue explains that the selected milestone no longer exists (or creates the issue without it), with no raw parser error.
bugs.actual: The server rejects the deleted milestone with a plain-text 404 'Not found.', and the page shows the toast: Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', "Not found." is not valid JSON. No issue is created; the draft stays on the page with the deleted milestone still selected. Clearing the milestone lets the issue be created.
reproSteps: Create a milestone in a repository.
Open New Issue, enter a title, select that milestone, and leave the draft unsaved.
In a second tab, delete that milestone from the Milestones page.
Return to the draft and click Create Issue.

bugs.name: Organization milestones: Sort > Name discards the repository filter
bugs.summary: On an organization's Milestones page, after excluding a repository with the sidebar filter, choosing Sort > Name brings the excluded repository's milestones back. The Name sort link doesn't carry the selected repositories.
bugs.expected: Changing the sort keeps the selected repository filter, so only the selected repositories' milestones are listed.
bugs.actual: With ORG-alpha excluded so only ORG-Beta-undated was listed, choosing Sort > Name listed ORG-Zebra-late, ORG-Beta-undated and ORG-Apple-early, and the open count went from 1 to 3.
reproSteps: In an organization with two repositories that each have a milestone, open the organization's Milestones page.
Click one repository in the sidebar filter to exclude it.
Choose Sort > Name.
Check whether the excluded repository's milestones are listed again.

relatedReference.name: Global milestones: Sort > Name discards the repository filter and restores excluded milestones
relatedReference.distinction: Same Name sort link and handler, but that entry is the global Milestones dashboard; this entry is an organization's Milestones page.

bugs.name: Alt+Enter in a milestone's Label filter includes the label instead of excluding it
bugs.summary: On a milestone's detail page, choosing a label in the Label filter with Alt+Enter includes it instead of excluding it, even though the filter's hint says Alt+click/Enter excludes labels.
bugs.expected: Alt+Enter on a label in the milestone's Label filter excludes that label, so issues without it, including unlabeled ones, stay listed.
bugs.actual: The label is applied as an include filter, so issues without it disappear and the milestone list can show No results.
reproSteps: Open a milestone that has issues without a particular label.
Open the Label filter on the milestone's detail page.
Search for that label, highlight it with the arrow keys, and press Alt+Enter.
Check whether the label was excluded or included, and whether the unlabeled issues are still listed.

relatedReference.name: Alt+Enter in the Label filter includes the label instead of excluding it
relatedReference.distinction: Same keyboard handling, but that entry is the repository Issues list; this entry is a milestone's detail page.

bugs.name: Global Milestones page shows a January 1, 1970 due date as '-'
bugs.summary: On the global Milestones page (/milestones), a milestone saved with a due date of January 1, 1970 shows '-' next to the calendar icon instead of the date, with or without a search. The saved date is correct; the page treats that date as no date.
bugs.expected: The global Milestones page shows the saved January 1, 1970 due date.
bugs.actual: The milestone's due date showed as '-' next to a calendar icon. Dates one day either side render normally, and editing the milestone shows the saved 1970-01-01 date.
reproSteps: Create or edit a milestone and set its due date to January 1, 1970.
Open Milestones from the top navigation (/milestones), optionally searching for the milestone.
Check the due date shown next to the calendar icon.

relatedReference.name: Milestone due date January 1, 1970 renders as '-' despite being saved
relatedReference.distinction: Same date and cause, but that entry is a repository's milestone list and detail page; this entry is the global Milestones page.

bugs.name: Milestone search treats underscores and percent signs as wildcards
bugs.summary: Milestone search passes the query to the database unescaped, so '_' matches any character and '%' matches anything. Searching QA_2027 also finds QA-2027, and searching % returns milestones with no percent sign, on both a repository's Milestones page and the global Milestones page.
bugs.expected: Milestone search treats '_' and '%' as literal characters, so it only returns milestones whose titles contain them.
bugs.actual: Searching QA_2027 returned both 'Literal QA_2027' and 'Literal QA-2027'; searching QA-2027 returned only the hyphenated one. Searching % returned every milestone, including titles without a percent sign.
reproSteps: Create milestones titled 'Literal QA_2027' and 'Literal QA-2027'.
On the repository's Milestones page, search for QA_2027 and note the results.
Search for QA-2027 and compare.
Search for % and check whether milestones without a percent sign are listed.

bugs.name: Creating an issue from a public milestone as a non-member shows a raw JSON error
bugs.summary: When a user who isn't a member or collaborator creates an issue from a public repository milestone's New Issue button, submitting fails with a red "Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', \"Not found.\" is not valid JSON" banner, which doesn't explain what went wrong or what to do.
bugs.expected: If the issue can't be created, the user sees a clear message saying why, such as not being allowed to set the milestone.
bugs.actual: Clicking Create Issue showed only the red network SyntaxError banner about "Not found." not being valid JSON; the form stayed unsaved.
reproSteps: As a user who isn't a member or collaborator of a public repository, open one of its milestones.
Click New Issue, fill in a title, and click Create Issue.
Read the error message shown.

relatedReference.name: Milestone page offers New Issue to users who can't create it with that milestone
relatedReference.distinction: Same failed create, but that entry is the New Issue button being offered and the create failing; this entry is the unhelpful raw JSON error shown for it.

bugs.name: Milestone page offers New Issue to users who can't create it with that milestone
bugs.summary: A public repository's milestone page shows New Issue to users who aren't members or collaborators. The button opens a form with the milestone preselected (but shown as No Milestone and locked), and Create Issue then fails. The user should either not be offered the button or be able to create the issue.
bugs.expected: A milestone's New Issue button is either hidden for users who can't create an issue with that milestone, or creating the issue from it works (for example without setting the milestone).
bugs.actual: As a non-member, the milestone page offered New Issue; the form showed No Milestone, and Create Issue failed without creating the issue. Creating an issue from the repository's normal New Issue page worked.
reproSteps: As a user who isn't a member or collaborator of a public repository, open one of its milestones.
Click New Issue and fill in a title.
Click Create Issue and check whether the issue was created.

relatedReference.name: Creating an issue from a public milestone as a non-member shows a raw JSON error
relatedReference.distinction: Same failed create, but that entry is the raw JSON error message; this entry is the New Issue button being offered and the create failing.

bugs.name: Rapid double-clicking Create Milestone creates duplicate milestones
bugs.summary: Two rapid clicks on Create Milestone during one completed form submission can insert two persistent milestones with identical titles and descriptions.
bugs.expected: A rapid accidental double-click during one milestone creation attempt creates one milestone, as the guarded New Issue form does. This does not require milestone names to be unique across deliberate creation attempts.
bugs.actual: With clicks about 50 ms apart, two distinct milestone records are inserted and listed after reload. Searching their title shows 2 Open and 0 Closed. A single-click control creates exactly one.
reproSteps: Open New Milestone in a writable repository and enter a fresh unique title and description.
Rapidly click Create Milestone twice, about 50 ms apart, before the first submission navigates away.
Search for the submitted title and confirm that two separate milestone links are listed with 2 Open and 0 Closed.
Open both records and reload the list to verify persistent duplicate records rather than duplicate rendering.
As a control, submit a fresh equivalent form with one click and confirm it creates exactly one record.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers duplicate persistent milestone creation from rapid repeated submission of one completed New Milestone form. Does not require mobile width. Deliberately submitting separate creation forms with the same title, or merely seeing repeated rendered rows without distinct saved IDs, is insufficient.
matchingGuidance.distinction: Duplicate labels created deliberately, stale compare forms creating duplicate pull requests, and retrying a blocked Close with Comment are separate triggers and causes.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user acceptance at severity 3 after both subscription-authenticated reviewers independently reproduced duplicate records and passing single-click controls. Both final verdicts recommend acceptance at severity 3.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Severity 3: unintended duplicate persistent records requiring manual cleanup, beyond a visual duplication.
analysis: Codex and Claude each reproduced twice at 390px with clicks 50 ms apart and verified separate saved milestone IDs. Both reproduced at desktop width and confirmed a single click creates one record. Codex additionally reproduced as a contributor.
Claude confirmed the guarded New Issue form creates one issue under the same 50 ms double-click. Codex confirmed repeating Update Milestone edits the existing record without creating another.
The milestone form is an ordinary POST without the shared fetch-action in-flight submission guard. Each valid creation request constructs a fresh milestone and inserts it in a transaction.
Claude also tested zero-gap Playwright dblclick and clicks 150 ms apart; those attempts created one milestone. Navigation timing and browser submit coalescing were inferred explanations, not traced.
Latest inspected source retains the ordinary form and insertion path; latest runtime was not tested.
limitations: Timing-sensitive: the sampled 50 ms double-clicks reproduced; zero-gap and 150 ms controls did not. No universal double-click failure rate is claimed.
One-record-per-attempt is an inferred data-integrity contract supported by the New Issue control; general milestone-name uniqueness is not required.
Latest runtime and repeated direct API requests were not tested.

bugs.name: Long milestone titles push the mobile Delete confirmation partly offscreen
bugs.summary: An unbroken milestone title widens the repository milestone list on mobile. Its Delete confirmation can centre on the widened layout viewport, clipping the right edge and part of the Yes button beyond the visible screen.
bugs.expected: The Delete Milestone confirmation and both buttons remain fully visible at phone width, even when a milestone title is long.
bugs.actual: At a visible width of 390px, mobile-emulated layout widths of 504–524px placed the dialog around x=77–428 or x=87–438. The Yes button extended past the visible right edge. Short or hyphenated titles and plain desktop viewport resizing kept the dialog onscreen.
reproSteps: Use a phone or mobile device emulation at about 390×844. The independent positive reproduction used touch and device scale factor 3; plain desktop viewport resizing passed as a control.
Create a disposable milestone with a roughly 48–50-character title containing a long unbroken run, such as LIFE- followed by consecutive digits.
On the repository milestone list, search for the title or its prefix and open Delete for that milestone.
Observe that the confirmation right edge and part of Yes lie outside the visible phone viewport.
As controls, repeat with short or hyphenated titles under the same mobile emulation, and with the long title under plain desktop viewport resizing; confirm the dialog fits.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing entry covers title and page overflow itself. This entry covers opening Delete afterward and the resulting offscreen confirmation. The accepted release-delete dialog has a different page-overflow trigger.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers the Delete confirmation and its Yes button clipping on mobile after a long milestone title widens the page. The user independently tested and accepted the bug. Plain desktop resizing passed as a control; it is not sufficient to disprove mobile behavior. Complete permanent inability to confirm deletion is not claimed because horizontal panning recovered the clipped portion in one reproduction.

reviewEvidence.basis: The user independently tested the bug and explicitly accepted it outright at severity 1. Claude also independently reproduced it twice with mobile device emulation and passing controls. Codex tested plain desktop viewport resizing, which passed; that different browser mode does not negate the confirmed mobile failure.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Severity 1: partially offscreen confirmation and button; no failed deletion request or saved-data loss demonstrated.
analysis: The user confirmed personal reproduction and requested outright acceptance. Acceptance is based on that confirmation and the positive independent mobile checks, rather than an override of non-reproduction.
Claude reproduced twice with isMobile, touch and DPR 3 at visible width 390px. The unbroken title widened the page/layout viewport, and the centred modal extended beyond the visible right edge.

Codex tested two fresh long titles and a control at 390px, plus 320px, desktop, open-dialog resizing and horizontal scrolling. Those plain viewport tests passed, and deletion succeeded. Claude also confirmed that plain resizing passes.

Pinned title markup lacks wrapping for unbroken runs. The fixed, inset dimmer centres the confirmation on the expanded layout viewport; the 90vw width cap alone does not keep it inside the narrower visible area.
Claude recovered the cut-off portion by horizontal wheel panning, so the observation is initial clipping rather than an established permanent navigation or deletion dead end.
Latest title styling adds overflow-wrap:anywhere and replaces the modal mechanism. A latest-runtime fix was not tested.
limitations: The user independently tested the bug; their exact device/browser setup was not specified.
Codex’s plain desktop viewport checks passed; independent positive runs used mobile device emulation.
Latest runtime, an exact upstream fixing commit and the original Mo recording were not independently verified.

bugs.name: Milestone detail page doesn't mark an overdue due date
bugs.summary: For an open milestone whose due date has passed, the milestone list shows the due date in red as overdue, but the milestone's own detail page shows the same date in the normal color with no overdue indication.
bugs.expected: The milestone detail page marks an overdue due date as overdue, consistent with the milestone list.
bugs.actual: A milestone due yesterday showed its date in red on the milestone list, but its detail page showed the date with no overdue styling.
reproSteps: Create a milestone with a due date in the past and leave it open.
On the repository's Milestones list, note that its due date is shown in red.
Open the milestone's detail page and check how the due date is shown.

bugs.name: Earliest due date milestone sort lists milestones without a due date first
bugs.summary: On a repository's Milestones list, the default sort and Sort > Earliest due date put milestones with no due date at the top, ahead of overdue and upcoming ones, while Latest due date puts them last.
bugs.expected: Sorting by earliest due date lists dated milestones from earliest to latest, with milestones that have no due date after them.
bugs.actual: With milestones due in 2025, November 2026 and December 2026 plus two with no due date, Earliest due date listed the two undated milestones first, then the dated ones.
reproSteps: Create several milestones with different due dates and at least one with no due date.
Open the repository's Milestones list with the default sort, or choose Sort > Earliest due date.
Check where the undated milestones appear.

bugs.name: Milestone search for text ending in % (like '100%') misses matching milestones
bugs.summary: Searching milestones for a term that ends (or starts) with % finds nothing even when a milestone's title contains that text: Gitea uses a search term that starts or ends with % as the raw match pattern instead of matching it anywhere in the title, so '100%' only matches titles that begin with 100. The repository, global and organization milestone lists are affected.
bugs.expected: Searching for '100%' lists milestones whose title contains '100%'.
bugs.actual: A milestone titled 'RL-Edge-100%_café & 日本語' was found by searching '100', but searching '100%' showed no milestones and 0 Open / 0 Closed.
reproSteps: Create a milestone whose title contains '100%' after other text.
On the Milestones list, search for '100', then for '100%'.
Compare the results.

relatedReference.name: Milestone search treats underscores and percent signs as wildcards
relatedReference.distinction: Same unescaped search pattern, but that entry is '_' and '%' over-matching other titles; this entry is a term ending or starting with '%' missing the titles that contain it.

bugs.name: Repository badge text runs over the milestone heading on mobile milestone lists
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, a milestone's repository badge on the organization and global milestone lists paints its text past the badge over the milestone icon and title, even for repository names around 31–38 characters.
bugs.expected: Repository badges on milestone rows fit, wrap or truncate without covering the milestone icon and title.
bugs.actual: On /org/<org>/milestones and /milestones at 390×844, a badge whose box ended at x=215 painted its text through x=360, over the icon at x=222–238 and the title at x=245–337. Repositories with short names and the same rows at 1024 and 1280 pixels render cleanly. Clicking the title still opens the milestone.
reproSteps: Create a repository whose full name (owner/repository) is about 35 characters or longer and add a milestone to it.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open the organization's Milestones page or the global Milestones page.
Observe the repository badge text running over the milestone icon and title.
bugs.sourceCause: templates/user/dashboard/milestones.tmpl puts the repository .ui.large.label in a flex heading, and web_src/css/modules/label.css makes .ui.label shrinkable (min-width:0) and nowrap with no overflow clipping, so its text paints past the shrunken box.

relatedReference.distinction: Same pages and cause. That entry was recorded with a repository name of about 60 characters; this entry is the same overlap from names of about 31–38 characters.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reports that a milestone row's repository badge text runs over the milestone icon or title on the organization or global Milestones lists match this entry at any narrow width (mobile or tablet), whether the badge is squeezed by a long repository name or by a long milestone title.

bugs.name: Global Milestones Sort > Name lists Zulu before Alpha
bugs.summary: On the global Milestones page (/milestones), choosing Sort > Name orders the listed milestones in reverse alphabetical order, so a search for two milestones named Alpha and Zulu shows Zulu first.
bugs.expected: Sort > Name lists Alpha before Zulu.
bugs.actual: After searching the global Milestones page for two new milestones sharing a prefix (Alpha and Zulu) and choosing Sort > Name, Zulu stayed above Alpha.
reproSteps: Create two milestones named <prefix> Alpha and <prefix> Zulu.
Open the global Milestones page from the top navigation and search for the prefix.
Choose Sort > Name.
Observe Zulu listed above Alpha.
bugs.sourceCause: models/issues/milestone_list.go maps the name sort to "name DESC", and the global Milestones page (routers/web/user/home.go Milestones) uses that order.

relatedReference.distinction: Same name DESC ordering. This entry is the global Milestones page at /milestones; the related entry was recorded on the repository Milestones list.

bugs.name: Organization Milestones Sort > Name orders milestones Z to A
bugs.summary: On an organization's Milestones page (/org/<org>/milestones), choosing Sort > Name lists milestones in reverse alphabetical order, unlike the usual A-to-Z meaning of a plain Name sort.
bugs.expected: Sort > Name lists milestones alphabetically from A to Z.
bugs.actual: On the organization's Milestones page, the default order was A to Z, and choosing Sort > Name changed it to Z to A (for example Zulu, Delta, Charlie, Bravo, Alpha).
reproSteps: In an organization repository, create milestones named Alpha, Delta and Zulu.
Open the organization's Milestones page from its dashboard.
Choose Sort > Name.
Observe Zulu listed first and Alpha last.
bugs.sourceCause: models/issues/milestone_list.go maps the name sort to "name DESC", and routers/web/user/home.go Milestones serves /org/<org>/milestones with that order.

relatedReference.distinction: Same name DESC ordering. This entry is the organization Milestones page; gitea-milestone-name-sort-descending is the repository list and gitea-global-milestone-name-sort-descending is the global /milestones page.
